idiom_name: single app_state struct + tagged action struct + pure reduce() + listener function pointers
implementation_notes: C has neither a component tree nor a store runtime, so the whole structure is hand-written: one translation unit owns the application state struct, actions are a tagged struct (an enum kind plus a payload), a pure reduce(const struct app_state *, const struct act *) returns the next state by value, and dispatch replaces the state and calls the registered listeners. Immutability is convention, not a compiler rule - reducers copy the incoming state and views only ever see a const snapshot, while nothing stops a stray cast from mutating shared memory. The classic structure is replaced by that convention plus an explicit notify step; it is still justified when a terminal or immediate-mode UI (or a test harness) must replay deterministic transitions, while a one-widget tool is better served by a plain state struct and a redraw call.
pitfalls: Handing out a pointer to the store's live state (instead of a copy or a const snapshot) lets views observe half-applied updates and lets anything mutate history away.
A listener array that only grows calls back into freed widgets after teardown; unregister on destroy and null-check the slots.
Reading a union member the action tag did not select is undefined behaviour even when the bits look right - switch on the tag before touching the payload.
Dispatching from a signal handler or ISR is not reentrant; queue the action and drain it from the main loop instead.
